subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Solid Lubricants: Dry and Slippery
description: One-minute skill: Solid Lubricants: Dry and Slippery.

hook.text: Some places are too hot or clean for oil. Dry lubricants fill the gap.

buildup.text: Graphite and MoS2 have layered crystals that slide past each other.

discovery.text: Weak bonds between layers let them shear easily with no liquid needed.

twist.text: Graphite needs moisture to work. In a vacuum it fails. MoS2 doesn't.

climax.text: Space mechanisms use MoS2 coatings. Oven hinges use graphite on Earth.

punchline.text: Slippery crystals work where oil can't survive.

quiz.question: Why does graphite fail as a lubricant in a vacuum?
options: It needs moisture between layers to enable easy sliding
Vacuum removes the oxide layer that makes graphite slippery
